newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC says covered on possible UK damages.
newsitem.headline: SBC says covered on possible UK damages.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp said its SBC Warburg investment banking unit had already booked in October any damages resulting from share transactions last year which are currently under investigation in Britain.
"I can assure you that any financial damages resulting from this (the transactions in question) were booked by SBC Warburg in October," SBC chief executive Marcel Ospel told a news conference.

Ospel declined to comment in any more detail on the case, saying it was still under investigation by the SFA. But he did confirm that the SFA had begun its investigation on the dealings, which took place in October.
"We have supported the SFA in its investigation in every way," Ospel said.
Earlier on Wednesday Britain's Securities and Futures Authority confirmed that it was investigating SBC Warburg, but it would make no further comment on the case.
The investigation is into the alleged mishandling of the sale of 300 million pounds of European shares for an investment trust.

Sources in Britain said the SFA investigation centred on the sharp fall of several European share prices in October after SBC Warburg carried out a series of share sales for Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
